title: How to Find and Fix the Causes of Your Bad Habits
coreMove: Trace a craving back to the underlying motive it is trying to serve, then reassign that motive to a response that actually delivers on it

exampleSpecs.domain: a night-shift ER nurse who reaches for the vending-machine pretzels every time a trauma case ends
exampleSpecs.audience: a healthcare worker whose 'bad habit' is masking an unmet need
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she keeps gaining weight she blames on shift work, when the real driver is needing two minutes of quiet she has never named
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse names the underlying motive — decompression after adrenaline — out loud, and notices the pretzels were never about hunger

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance illustrator who opens Instagram every time a client email arrives
exampleSpecs.audience: a solo creative professional whose phone use is eating her billable hours
exampleSpecs.stakes: a contract that pays her rent, now two weeks behind because each email triggers a forty-minute scroll
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she pauses before the unlock, asks what the scroll is actually doing for her, and identifies dread of the email's contents as the real cue

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional bakery manager and his assistant talking through why he yells at the morning crew on delivery days
exampleSpecs.audience: a frontline manager who thinks his temper is a personality trait
exampleSpecs.stakes: a head baker about to quit over the yelling, and a wholesale account he cannot afford to lose
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the assistant walks him through the prediction his brain is making before each outburst, and he reframes the yelling as a forecast of failure rather than a moral flaw

exampleSpecs.domain: a divorced father reviewing the week he spent every evening reorganizing his garage instead of calling his teenage daughter
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent whose avoidance habit looks like productivity
exampleSpecs.stakes: a relationship with a sixteen-year-old who is one summer away from leaving for college
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he traces the garage work back to the prediction that the call will go badly, and assigns a smaller response — a two-line text — to the same underlying motive of staying connected

exampleSpecs.domain: a graduate student in chemistry who pours a glass of wine the moment she closes her laptop each night
exampleSpecs.audience: an early-career researcher who has read enough to know the wine is not helping her sleep
exampleSpecs.stakes: a dissertation defense in eleven weeks and mornings she increasingly cannot use
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she sits with the question of what the first sip is predicting for her, and names the prediction as 'permission to stop being responsible' rather than relaxation

exampleSpecs.domain: imagine you are a city bus driver who buys a scratch ticket at the end of every route, and you have just been told the habit costs you four hundred dollars a month
exampleSpecs.audience: the reader, placed inside the example
exampleSpecs.stakes: a daughter's tuition payment that is now six weeks late
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reader is asked to write down what the scratch ticket is actually delivering — a sliver of possibility at the end of a fixed route — before being shown how to redirect that craving
